issues.description: Conditional gating logic is awkwardly written and reads poorly
issues.detail: The expression `not self.get_conf(...) and not key == Qt.Key_Tab` mixes a negated config lookup with `not key == Qt.Key_Tab` instead of the more readable `key != Qt.Key_Tab`. For code that lives inside a `keyPressEvent` and decides whether to swallow vs. forward a key, the reader needs to immediately see the invariant: 'if Enter-to-accept is disabled and the user did not press Tab, defer to the editor.' Rewrite as a guarded early-return with a literate comment stating that invariant; the current form forces the reader to mentally re-associate the `not` operators.

issues.description: Gate fires for every key, including Escape, arrows, Backspace, and modifier keys
issues.detail: The new branch sits at the top of the Return/Enter handling block but its condition only excludes Tab. As written, when `use_enter_for_completions` is False, any key other than Tab that reaches this branch will hide the popup and re-dispatch the event to the textedit. The author needs to state the invariant for which keys this branch is supposed to govern (Enter/Return only) and restrict the condition accordingly, e.g. `key in (Qt.Key_Return, Qt.Key_Enter)`. Without that, the option silently changes behavior for navigation keys that were previously handled below.

issues.description: Re-dispatching the same QKeyEvent back to the textedit is under-audited
issues.detail: Calling `self.textedit.keyPressEvent(event)` after `self.hide()` re-enters the editor's key handler with an event the popup has already consumed in its own handler. The author should state the termination/reentrancy invariant: this cannot loop, the event's `accepted` flag is in the expected state, and the editor will treat a re-delivered Enter exactly as it would a fresh keystroke (including auto-indent and any completion-trigger side effects). A one-line comment establishing that, plus a test, would move this from UNDER-AUDITED to RIGOROUS.

issues.description: Per-keystroke config lookup with no comment on cost
issues.detail: `self.get_conf(...)` is called on every keypress inside the completion popup. Almost certainly negligible compared to a human typing rate, so this is PREMATURE-OPTIMIZATION territory to fix; flagging only so the author can note in a comment that the lookup is intentionally simple and not cached. If profiling ever shows it, cache via a config-change subscription.

issues.description: Missing literate comment explaining the new branch
issues.detail: The new block has no comment. For a keyPressEvent branch whose entire purpose is a user-facing behavior toggle tied to issue #12728, a two-line comment naming the option, the keys it governs, and why the event is re-dispatched would make the code readable as documentation. NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT.

issues.description: No test accompanies the behavior change
issues.detail: Beware of bugs in the above code; I have only proved it correct, not tried it. A small test that exercises both states of `use_enter_for_completions` against Return, Enter, and Tab keypresses would catch the over-broad condition flagged above and document the intended invariant for future maintainers.

review.summary: The change is small and the intent is clear, but the new branch in `completion.py` is UNDER-AUDITED on two fronts: its condition is `not ... and not key == Qt.Key_Tab`, which both reads poorly and is too permissive — it will fire for any non-Tab key that reaches this Return/Enter handler, not just Enter/Return as the option name implies. The re-dispatch of the same QKeyEvent back to `self.textedit.keyPressEvent` also needs a stated invariant about non-reentrancy and event-accepted state. Config plumbing and the preference UI look fine. A literate two-line comment stating the invariant ("when Enter-to-accept is off, forward Enter/Return to the editor; Tab still accepts"), a tightened key check, and one test covering Return/Enter/Tab under both option states would move this from UNDER-AUDITED to RIGOROUS.
